lessons.title: Story Time: A Spring Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss changes described in a spring-themed story.
success_criteria: I can say what changed in the story.
I can name a sign of spring.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss signs of spring noticed recently.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a spring-themed story, modelling discussion of change and growth.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about changes described in the story.
key_questions: What sign of spring is this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of change/growth theme — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap signs of spring in the story.
lessons.home_link: Look for a sign of spring outside.

lessons.title: Measuring Plant Growth in Centimetres
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and record plant height using standard units.
success_criteria: I can measure using a ruler.
I can record the height in cm.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap measuring in cm from Week 12.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring a plant's height using a ruler and recording in a growth chart.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure plant/seedling heights using a ruler, recording in cm.
key_questions: How tall is this plant in cm?

differentiation.greater_depth: Measure multiple plants and compare growth rates

lessons.assessment_notes: Record standard unit measuring applied to a science investigation — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure a plant at home with a ruler if you have one.

lessons.title: Signs of Spring Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of spring, extending Year 1 learning.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of spring.
I can compare spring to winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of spring (warmer weather, flowers blooming, new leaves, baby animals), comparing to winter.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label signs of spring, comparing to winter features.
key_questions: What is different about spring compared to winter?
What signs of spring can you see?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare spring to winter in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note extension of seasonal change understanding from Year 1 — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Look for signs of spring with your family.

lessons.title: Writing a Plant Growth Diary Entry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a diary entry describing plant growth using the present tense.
success_criteria: I can describe my plant's growth.
I can use the present tense consistently.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a diary entry in the present tense describing current plant growth.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own plant diary entry using consistent present tense.
key_questions: What does your plant look like now?
Is your writing in the present tense?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note diary writing with tense consistency (present, contrasting with past tense used elsewhere) — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Write about a plant you're growing or have seen.

lessons.title: Counting in Multiples: Petals and Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in steps of 2, 3, 5 and 10 using a plant context.
success_criteria: I can count in steps.
I can find a total.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting in steps from Week 13.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting flower petals/seeds in steps of 2, 3, 5 and 10.
lessons.independent_task: Children count plant-themed counters in steps, recording totals.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record consolidation of counting in steps, including 3s (new for Year 2) — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count petals or seeds at home.

lessons.title: How Do Seeds and Bulbs Grow?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how seeds and bulbs grow into plants.
success_criteria: I can describe how a seed grows.
I can describe how a bulb grows.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real seed and a real bulb, discussing differences.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how seeds germinate and bulbs sprout, comparing the two growth processes.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare growing from a seed and growing from a bulb, recording similarities/differences.
resources_needed: Seed and bulb picture cards/real examples

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning for the comparison

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of different plant growth processes, a Year 2 objective — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Look at a seed or bulb at home if available.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Spring Growth Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read spring-growth-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read growth words.
I can read a sentence about growth.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to growth-themed words (e.g. 'sprout', 'bulb', 'shoot').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading growth words over the week.

lessons.title: Multiplication: Planting in Rows
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent multiplication using arrays of planted seeds.
success_criteria: I can create an array.
I can write the multiplication sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating arrays representing seeds planted in rows (e.g. 4 rows of 5 seeds).
lessons.independent_task: Children create arrays using seed counters and write matching multiplication sentences.

differentiation.support: Create arrays for 2 and 10 times tables
differentiation.greater_depth: Create arrays for 2, 3, 5 and 10 times tables

lessons.assessment_notes: Record array representation of multiplication applied to a growing context — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Find an array of objects at home and write the multiplication sentence.

lessons.title: Planting Our Own Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plant a seed correctly and predict its growth.
success_criteria: I can plant a seed correctly.
I can predict what will happen.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what seeds need to germinate.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model planting a seed correctly (depth, soil, watering).
lessons.independent_task: Children plant their own seed, predicting and recording what they think will happen.
key_questions: How deep should you plant the seed?
What do you predict will happen?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical planting skill and prediction, beginning an ongoing observation for next week — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Recap seeds planted and predictions made.
lessons.home_link: Help plant a seed at home if possible.

lessons.title: Discussing Plant Growth Predictions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss and justify a prediction about plant growth.
success_criteria: I can state my prediction.
I can give a reason for it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating a prediction with reasoning.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss their planting predictions in small groups, giving reasons.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note scientific reasoning and discussion skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of predictions shared.
lessons.home_link: Discuss your planting prediction with your family.

lessons.title: Spring Growth Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a spring growth context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a growth context (e.g. plant grows 3cm more each week).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve growth-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: How tall will it be after another week?
How much has it grown altogether?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a growth word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Baby Animals in Spring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name baby animals commonly seen in spring.
success_criteria: I can name a baby animal seen in spring.
I can say why spring is a common birth time.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss baby animals associated with spring (lambs, chicks, ducklings).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why many animals are born in spring (more food available, warmer weather).
lessons.independent_task: Children record baby animals seen in spring and why this timing helps them.
key_questions: Why might spring be a good time to be born?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning about food availability and survival

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cross-curricular link between seasonal change and animal life cycles — evidence for SCI.SEA/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look for baby animals in spring near your home.

lessons.title: Spring Changes and Plant Growth Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about spring changes and plant growth.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about spring and plant growth, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why are baby animals often born in spring?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on spring facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Multiples, Arrays, Measuring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting in multiples, array, and measuring skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count in multiples.
I can use an array.
I can measure in cm.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of counting in multiples, arrays, and measuring.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 26 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N3/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting in multiples over the weekend.

lessons.title: Spring Changes and Plant Growth Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about spring changes and plant growth so far.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of spring.
I can describe how seeds/bulbs grow.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering spring signs, seed/bulb growth, and spring baby animals.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Spring Changes' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about spring?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note seasonal and plant growth understanding progress, setting up deeper plant needs learning next week — evidence for SCI.PLA/SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about spring with your family.
